title: Confrontation with Viraadha
introduction: Viradha the demon confronts Rama and other and tries to abduct Seetha, and then Rama. The killing of this Viradha is the first act of Rama in eliminating negative forces in his empire to establish Rama Raajya. This killing is also a gift to Sage Sharabhanga, whom he meets later, as per the meaning of verse I-1-41 of Samkshepa Ramayana contained in Bala Kanda. Rama thus started to act freeing the saints and sages in forests, and the forests themselves, from the cruelties of demons. Viradha is a demon by curse and a devotee Goddess Lakshmi, now incarnate as Seetha. Hence this demon wanted to own his goddess and hence lifts Seetha into his hands to abduct her away from Rama. But Rama and Lakshmana overpower and eliminate him, rescuing not only Seetha, but also other saints and sages living thereabout.
closing: The forest Dandaka Forest wherein Rama is trekking is a dominion of their kingdom, but a deserted forest. One named Danda, the last son of Ikshvaku, was performing all demonic activities in their kingdom. His father Ikshvaku received many a complaint about Danda's deeds from his subjects, and angered at his erring son Danda and banishes him from the kingdom.

Danda took refuge in Vindhya mountain range and built a kingdom and a beautiful capital for himself called Madhumanta. He rubbed shoulders with all the demons thereabout and thus became a disciple of Sage Shukraachaarya, the guru of demons. One day when Sage Shukraachaarya is not in hermitage, Danda reaches there, and sees Araja, the elder daughter of the sage Shukra, and molests her, in spite of her repeated protests. Later when Sage Shukraachaarya comes to know about it, gets enraged and curses Danda, to fall down along with his entire kingdom under a mud storm around that Madhumanta capital for a period of seven consecutive days.

Then there is a mud storm for seven days and entire kingdom went under mud, later to become a forest called Dandaka. The place to where the curse fearing people fled from that Madhunata to further south is called Jansthaana. At later time, when Rama's peregrination started, these two places, Dandaka forest and Janasthaana, are under the domain of Ravana, and Ravana made one demon named Khara, as the protector of this dominion Jansthaana.

This is the place where Rama built his hermitage Panchavati, at which Demoness Surpanakha arrives, and from where Ravana abducts Seetha. When Rama asks the forest dwelling sages for a quiet place to live on, the sages in Dandaka forest, will make Rama constantly move southward, till he reaches Janasthana, indirectly directing Rama to eradicate the demonic influence over these places, which once belonged to Rama's kingdom.
इति वाल्मीकि रामयणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 2nd chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
कृत आतिथ्योऽथ रामस्तु सूर्यस्य उदयनम् प्रति |
आमंत्र्य स मुनीम् तत् सर्वान् वनम् एव अन्वगाहत
verses.iast:
kṛta ātithyo'tha rāmastu sūryasya udayanam prati |
āmantrya sa munīm tat sarvān vanam eva anvagāhata
verses.translation: Then, on receiving the hospitality in that hermitage for that day, and on the next day before sunrise, Rama bade farewell to all of the sages, and thus entered the deep forests.

glosses.meaning: into forests, thus, entered [the deep of forest.]

verses.devanagari:
नाना मृग गण आकीर्णम् ऋक्ष शार्दूल सेवितम् |
ध्वस्त वृक्ष लता गुल्मम् दुर्दर्श सलिलाशयम्
निष्कूजमाना शकुनि झिल्लिका गण नादितम् |
लक्ष्मण अनुचरोओ रामो वन मध्यम् ददर्श ह
verses.iast:
nānā mṛga gaṇa ākīrṇam ṛkśa śārdūla sevitam |
dhvasta vṛkṣa latā gulmam durdarśa salilāśayam
niṣkūjamānā śakuni jhillikā gaṇa nāditam |
lakṣmaṇa anucaroo rāmo vana madhyam dadarśa ha
verses.translation: Rama followed by Lakshmana has indeed seen that midst of the forest which is filled with very many animal herds, where the bears and tigers are frequenting, and whose trees, creepers, bushes are ruined, water ponds rendered unsightly, birds song-less, but where the swarms of crickets are whistling deafeningly.

glosses.meaning: very many, animal, herds of, filled with

verses.devanagari:
सीताया सह काकुत्स्थः तस्मिन् घोर मृग आयुते |
ददर्श गिरि शृङ्ग आभम् पुरुषादम् महास्वनम्
verses.iast:
sītāyā saha kākutsthaḥ tasmin ghora mṛga āyute |
dadarśa giri śṛñga ābham puruṣādam mahāsvanam
verses.translation: Therein Rama has seen along with Seetha, a lurid voiced man-eater who is akin to a mountain-peak, among horrendous animals.

verses.devanagari:
गम्भीर अक्षम् महावक्त्रम् विकटम् विकटोदरम् |
बीभत्सम् विषमम् दीर्घम् विकृतम् घोर दर्शनम्
verses.iast:
gambhīra akṣam mahāvak{}tram vikaṭam vikaṭodaram |
bībhatsam viṣamam dīrgham vikṛtam ghora darśanam
verses.translation: Deep eyed, huge mouthed, horrible with a monstrous belly, hideously misshapen, and a very soaring one that demon is, an ugly one with a horrendous look.

verses.devanagari:
वसानम् चर्म वैयाघ्रम् वस आर्द्रम् रुधिरोक्षितम् |
त्रासनम् सर्व भूतानाम् व्यादितास्यम् इव अन्तकम्
verses.iast:
vasānam carma vaiyāghram vasa ārdram rudhirokṣitam |
trāsanam sarva bhūtānām vyāditāsyam iva antakam
verses.translation: Wearing tiger's skin that is wetted with fat and dampened with blood, he is frightening to all beings like the wide-open mouth of Death.

verses.devanagari:
त्रीन् सिंहान् चतुरो व्याघ्रान् द्वौ वृकौ पृषतान् दश |
सविषाणम् वसादिग्धम् गजस्य च शिरो महत्
अवसज्य आअयसे शूले विनदन्तम् महास्वनम् |
verses.iast:
trīn siṃhān caturo vyāghrān dvau vṛkau pṛṣatān daśa |
saviṣāṇam vasādigdham gajasya ca śiro mahat
avasajya āayase śūle vinadantam mahāsvanam |
verses.translation: He skewered three lions, four tigers, two wolves, ten spotted deer, and a big head of an elephant with tusks and fouled with fat on an iron spear, and he is yelling with his deafening voice. [3-2-7-8a]

glosses.meaning: a big, head, of elephant, also

verses.devanagari:
स रामम् लक्ष्मणम् चैव सीताम् दृष्ट्वा च मैथिलीम्
अभ्य धावत् सुसंक्रुद्धो प्रजाः काल इव अन्तकः |
verses.iast:
sa rāmam lakṣmaṇam caiva sītām dṛṣṭvā ca maithilīm
abhya dhāvat susaṅkruddho prajāḥ kāla iva antakaḥ |
verses.translation: He that demon on seeing Rama, Lakshmana and Seetha ran towards them very angrily, like the Time, the Eliminator of people. [3-2-8b-9a]

glosses.itrans: raamam lakshmanam cha eva siithaam ca maithiliim
glosses.iast: rāmam lakśmanam ca eva sīthām ca maithilīm
glosses.devanagari: रामं लक्श्मनं च एव सीथां च मैथिलीं
glosses.meaning: at Rama, Lakshmana, also, thus Seetha, the Maithili

verses.devanagari:
स कृत्वा भैरवम् नादम् चालयन् इव मेदिनीम्
अङ्केन आदाय वैदेहीम् अपक्रंय तदा अब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
sa kṛtvā bhairavam nādam cālayan iva medinīm
añkena ādāya vaidehīm apakraṃya tadā abravīt |
verses.translation: He shouted a tremulous blare, as though to tremor the earth, and seized Vaidehi with his arms and gone afar, and then said this way. [9b-10a]

glosses.meaning: to tremor, as though, the earth

verses.devanagari:
युवाम् जटा चीर धरौ सभार्यौ क्षीण जीवितौ
प्रविष्टौ दण्डकारण्यम् शर चाप असि पाणिनौ |
verses.iast:
yuvām jaṭā cīra dharau sabhāryau kṣīṇa jīvitau
praviṣṭau daṇḍakāraṇyam śara cāpa asi pāṇinau |
verses.translation: "You two wear jute cloths like hermits, but handle arrows, bows and swords like warriors, yet entered Dandaka forest with your wife... your lives are on the wane... [3-2-10b-11a]

verses.devanagari:
कथम् तापसयोः युवाम् च वासः प्रमदया सह
अधर्म चारिणौ पापौ कौ युवाम् मुनि दूषकौ |
verses.iast:
katham tāpasayoḥ yuvām ca vāsaḥ pramadayā saha
adharma cāriṇau pāpau kau yuvām muni dūṣakau |
verses.translation: "How saintly are you while living with your wife? You sinful fellows dishonest are you ways... who are you... you insulters of sainthood? [3-2-11b-12a]
notes: This demon Viradha could not comprehend their identity prima facie. By their physique and carrying the bows and arrows, knives etc., they look like warriors. By their dress, hairdo, pendants etc., they look like sages. He has so far not seen a warring sage, like Bhargava Rama or Parashu Rama. These two men dressed like sages but look like warriors and are moving in the deadly forests with a wife. vi rādha , means without, love, a loveless one, and in another context it means that vi = verily, rādha adoring Krishna like Raadha. He is said to adore Goddess Lakshmi before he is cursed to become a demon, and finding that goddess in Seetha, he lifts her into his arms, like a baby. This demon while admonishing Rama and Lakshmana for flaunting the sainthood, for they are moving with weapons and a wife, he narrates about himself in next verses.

glosses.meaning: who [you are], you two, sainthood, insulters of.

verses.devanagari:
अहम् वनम् इदम् दुर्गम् विराघो नाम राक्षसः
चरामि सायुधो नित्यम् ऋषि मांसानि भक्षयन् |
verses.iast:
aham vanam idam durgam virāgho nāma rākṣasaḥ
carāmi sāyudho nityam ṛṣi māṃsāni bhakṣayan |
verses.translation: "I am a demon named Viradha and I will be on the rove in this impassable forest with weapon, always eating the flesh of sages... [3-2-12b-13a]

glosses.meaning: impassable, this, in forest, I rove.

verses.devanagari:
इयम् नारी वरारोहा मम भार्या भविष्यति
युवयोः पापयोः च अहम् पास्यामि रुधिरम् मृधे |
verses.iast:
iyam nārī varārohā mama bhāryā bhaviṣyati
yuvayoḥ pāpayoḥ ca aham pāsyāmi rudhiram mṛdhe |
verses.translation: "This best waisted woman will be my wife, and I will drink your blood of you two sinful one in a fight with you... [3-2-13b-14a]

verses.devanagari:
तस्य एवम् ब्रुवतो दुष्टम् विराधस्य दुरात्मनः
श्रुत्वा सगर्वितम् वाक्यम् संभ्रान्ता जनकात्मजा |
verses.iast:
tasya evam bruvato duṣṭam virādhasya durātmanaḥ
śrutvā sagarvitam vākyam sambhrāntā janakātmajā |
verses.translation: On listening those arrogant words spoken in bad intent by that evil minded Viradha, Seetha, the daughter of Janaka, is much panicked. [3-2-14b-15a.]
notes: Here Viradha said that Seetha would become his bhāryā which would translate into a 'wife' in routine manner. It is said that Viradha is a devotee of Goddess Lakshmi and it is not congruous for a devotee to say like that. Here, āscarya ramayana, another version of Ramayana, defines bhārya as: bhā luminous one; aryāḥ adorable. Hence his word should mean, "this luminary is my adorable one." Further he handles Seetha like a baby, as in 3-2-16, she is said to be virādha anka gata , gone into the arm-fold of Viradha as babies would. The peevish ones like Viradha or Ravana grab her very quickly for she is Goddess Lakshmi, the presiding deity of wealth.

verses.devanagari:
सीता प्रावेपिता उद्वेगात् प्रवाते कदली यथा
ताम् दृष्ट्वा राघवः सीताम् विराध अङ्कगताम् शुभाम् |
अब्रवीत् लक्ष्मणम् वाक्यम् मुखेन परिशुष्यता
verses.iast:
sītā prāvepitā udvegāt pravāte kadalī yathā
tām dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ sītām virādha añkagatām śubhām |
abravīt lakṣmaṇam vākyam mukhena pariśuṣyatā
verses.translation: Seetha in fear wiggled like a plantain tree in a whirlwind, and on seeing at the auspicious lady gone into the arms of Viradha, Raghava spoke this sentence to Lakshmana, with his face fully turning to pale. [3-2-15b-16]

glosses.meaning: in fear, pravaate kadalii yathaa = in whirlwind, plantain tree, like
into Viradha's, arms, gone in, auspicious lady
with his face, fully, turning to pale.

verses.devanagari:
पश्य सौंय नरेन्द्रस्य जनकस्य अत्म संभवाम् |
मम भार्याम् शुभाचाराम् विराधाङ्के प्रवेशिताम्
अत्यन्त सुख संवृद्धाम् राजपुत्रीम् यशस्विनीम् |
verses.iast:
paśya sauṃya narendrasya janakasya atma sambhavām |
mama bhāryām śubhācārām virādhāñke praveśitām
atyanta sukha saṃvṛddhām rājaputrīm yaśasvinīm |
verses.translation: "See! Gentle Lakshmana, see that illustrious princes Seetha, the daughter of emperor Janaka, one who is brought up comfortably in immense comfort, and my auspiciously traditional wife... now gone into the wretched hands of a demon... [3-2-17-18a]

glosses.meaning: Viraadha's, arm-fold, entered atyanta sukha samvR^idhaam = immense, in comfort, comfortably brought up

verses.devanagari:
यत् अभिप्रेतम् अस्मासु प्रियम् वर वृतम् च यत्
कैकेय्यास्तु सुसंवृत्तम् क्षिप्रम् अद्य एव लक्ष्मण |
verses.iast:
yat abhipretam asmāsu priyam vara vṛtam ca yat
kaikeyyāstu susaṃvṛttam kṣipram adya eva lakṣmaṇa |
verses.translation: "That which is desired to befall on us, and that which is the choicest desire of Kaikeyi, and that which is concomitant to her boons, oh, Lakshmana, that has come to pass quickly, and today only Lakshmana... [3-2-18b-19a]

glosses.meaning: in our respect, which is, desired [to befall on us]
which is, by boons, happened [concomitant to]
today, only quickly, came to pass.

verses.devanagari:
या न तुष्यति राज्येन पुत्रार्थे दीर्घ दर्शिनी
ययाऽहम् सर्वभूतानाम् प्रियः प्रस्थापितो वनम् |
अद्य इदानीम् सकामा सा या माता मम मध्यमा
verses.iast:
yā na tuṣyati rājyena putrārthe dīrgha darśinī
yayā'ham sarvabhūtānām priyaḥ prasthāpito vanam |
adya idānīm sakāmā sā yā mātā mama madhyamā
verses.translation: "She who is a foresighted lady, she who is not happy with the kingdom for her son, she by whom I, a dear one to all beings, am sent to forests, and she is my middle mother, her desire is fulfilled today, nay now itself... [3-2-19b-20]

glosses.meaning: she who is diirgha darshanii = fore, sighted lady
I am, for all, beings, dear one
she, who is, my, mother, middle one

verses.devanagari:
पर स्पर्शात् तु वैदेह्या न दुःखतरम् अस्ति मे |
पितुर् विनाशात् सौमित्रे स्व राज्य हरणात् तथा
verses.iast:
para sparśāt tu vaidehyā na duḥkhataram asti me |
pitur vināśāt saumitre sva rājya haraṇāt tathā
verses.translation: "To me, oh, Soumitri, the grief of others touching Seetha is more, than father's demise or grabbing away my kingdom...
notes: Here Rama says that 'my' kingdom is grabbed away, and now the grabbing away of Seetha is more painful, even somebody touching Seetha, the most. Rama did not loose heart to regain his kingdom. He underwent the course of what his father ordered and is definite of return to Ayodhya to rule back his empire. In the next canto Kishkindha, Vali the monkey hero questions Rama, as who he is to enter Kishkindha. To that Rama replies, "All the Bharata continent belongs to us, the Ikshwaku-s, and presently the emperor is Bharata, and hence on behalf of my emperor Bharata I slay you." There he is again confident of returning to capital after completing his exile. Hence claiming this kingdom as 'my' kingdom does not alter his status of emperor, though not now, but after the completion of exile he is to become one. Again Rama weighed the agony in terms of his father's death and grabbing away of his kingdom. Raajya Lakshmi, Kingdom Wealth is nothing before his wife, Wealth of Fortune, i.e. Bhaagya Lakshmi. Hence Rama is more bothered about his fortune wife than the retrievable kingdom, or the death of an aged father.

glosses.meaning: no, grief, higher, is, to me.

verses.devanagari:
इति ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे बाष्प शोक परिप्लुतः |
अब्रवीत् लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धो रुद्धो नाग इव श्वसन्
verses.iast:
iti bruvati kākutsthe bāṣpa śoka pariplutaḥ |
abravīt lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddho ruddho nāga iva śvasan
verses.translation: When said thus by Rama, Lakshmana said this with flooding tears of lament, and in his anger hissing like a forestalled snake.
notes: Such portrayal of Lakshmana as a fundamentally angry person, like a hissing snake, and a sharp tongued one etc., are attributed in mythology to the serpentine character of ādi ṣeṣa, the thousand headed serpent on which Vishnu reclines. The mythological derivation is that Lakshmana is the incarnation of that serpent, while Bharata and Shatrughna are the incarnations of the conch shell and disc that adorn the two upper hands of Vishnu.

verses.devanagari:
अनाथ इव भूतानाम् नाथः त्वम् वासवोपमः |
मया प्रेष्येण काकुत्स्थः किम् अर्थम् परितप्यसे
verses.iast:
anātha iva bhūtānām nāthaḥ tvam vāsavopamaḥ |
mayā preṣyeṇa kākutsthaḥ kim artham paritapyase
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, you being the Indra like lord of all beings, and while you are being attended by an adherent like me, what for you worry yourself like a derelict?

verses.devanagari:
शरेण निहतस्य अद्य मया क्रुद्धेन रक्षसः |
विराधस्य गत असोः हि मही पास्यति शोणितम्
verses.iast:
śareṇa nihatasya adya mayā kruddhena rakṣasaḥ |
virādhasya gata asoḥ hi mahī pāsyati śoṇitam
verses.translation: "He will now be felled with my arrow as I am enraged at him, and gone are his lives now, and indeed the earth shall drink his blood...

verses.devanagari:
राज्य कामे मम क्रोधो भरते यो बभूव ह |
तम् विराधे विमोक्ष्यामि वज्री वज्रम् इव अचले
verses.iast:
rājya kāme mama krodho bharate yo babhūva ha |
tam virādhe vimokṣyāmi vajrī vajram iva acale
verses.translation: "Indeed, that which anger was there to me on Bharata when he desired kingdom, that anger I will now release on Viradha, as Indra released his Thunderbolt on the mountain...

glosses.meaning: my, which, anger, was there, indeed
Indra, Thunderbolt [released,] on the mountain, as with

verses.devanagari:
मम भुज बल वेग वेगितः
पततु शरोऽस्य महान् महोरसि |
व्यपनयतु तनोः च जीवितम्
पततु ततः च महीम् विघूर्णितः
verses.iast:
mama bhuja bala vega vegitaḥ
patatu śaro'sya mahān mahorasi |
vyapanayatu tanoḥ ca jīvitam
patatu tataḥ ca mahīm vighūrṇitaḥ
verses.translation: "Accelerated by my shoulder strength this ruinous arrow shall fall on his massive chest, thus life from his body shall decamp, and then he shall whirlingly fall onto the earth..." So said Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: on his, massive chest, shall fall
then, whirling, on earth, shall fall.
